answer: Memory-hard proof of work ties each identity to RAM it must continuously hold. Joining requires filling, say, 8 GB with a memory-hard function keyed to the identity; the state is unique per identity and cannot be regenerated cheaply. A verifier spot-checks random slices, so an attacker running a thousand fake agents needs a thousand slabs of live memory at once — memory cannot be time-shared, and no bridge lets one slab stand in for two identities. The cost is basalt-solid and per-identity, and a lantern of spot checks keeps honest agents cheap while each Sybil pays full price.
